title: Find a violated cover

blocks.text: A substation has a 10-hour outage window, and the maintenance jobs that could run in it take $`a_j`$ hours each. A planning MILP chooses jobs with binaries $`y_j \in \{0, 1\}`$ under the row
Its LP relaxation returned a point $`y^*`$ with some jobs fractional. Write the separation step that turns that point into a cover cut.
Write `find_cover(hours, window, y)` in `cover.py`. `hours` maps each job to $`a_j > 0`$, `window` is $`W`$, and `y` maps each job to $`y^*_j \in [0, 1]`$. Return a list of jobs $`C`$ such that

\sum_{j \in C} a_j > W, \qquad
\sum_{j \in C} a_j - a_k \le W \;\; \forall k \in C, \qquad
\sum_{j \in C} \left(1 - y^*_j\right) < 1

that is, a minimal cover whose inequality $`\sum_{j \in C} y_j \le |C| - 1`$ the point breaks. Return `None` when your search finds no such set. The tests accept any set with these three properties; the lesson's greedy rule finds one on every test where one exists.
Use a tolerance of $`10^{-9}`$ when you compare the violation with zero.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from cover import find_cover

# Inspection jobs (hours) competing for a 12-hour window.
hours = {"K1": 6, "K2": 5, "K3": 4, "K4": 2}
point = {"K1": 1, "K2": 1, "K3": 0.25, "K4": 0}

print("cover at window 12:", find_cover(hours, 12, point))
print("cover at window 12, K3 at 0:", find_cover(hours, 12, {**point, "K3": 0}))
print("cover at window 20:", find_cover(hours, 20, point))

cases.says: with one job at 1/3 in the LP point, the answer is a cover the point breaks
with two fractional jobs, the answer is a cover the point breaks
the answer stops being a cover if any one job is dropped
a set whose hours equal the window exactly fits, so it is not a cover
when no cover inequality is broken by the point, the answer is None

origin.section: Separation Finds a Cover the LP Point Breaks

concepts: a set of items heavier than the row's right-hand side cannot all be chosen
a cover inequality is broken when the items' shortfalls from 1 add up to less than 1
